speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I need to understand your symptoms to proceed; do you have any new skin lesions, rashes, or changes in existing moles that you are concerned about?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

The combination of non-healing, crusty lesions on the penis and finger in a 62-year-old male smoker, unresponsive to prior treatments for syphilis and eczema, is highly suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma. Given the potential for malignancy, I will now request specific imaging and biopsy results to confirm the diagnosis and stage the disease.
